helpers.role: Existing Windows task XML physical storage owner used by Product recovery.
observed_contract: Creates windows-product-pair-task-rollback-* beneath stateDir and captures parent/root native identities.
Retain writes task-<SHA-256>.xml via WriteStateFileBytesAtomic, then no-follow hash/byte readback; Load requires known ref.
Acquisition/operation failures wrap and retain the original store.
Close is selected discard: captures original root, removes attempted XML/.lock leaf paths, then deletes the same retained native root.
No idle native handles when material is simply retained.
limits: Windows-only and tied to Product recovery namespace/reopen conventions.
Captured directory identities do not prove immutable identity of each XML leaf; writer is replace-capable after a pathname existence check.
Close removes tracked leaf paths, not separately retained leaf handles.
MkdirTemp plus Chmod(0700) alone does not prove Windows directory DACL privacy; per-file hardened writer is the byte-privacy boundary.
Storage alone does not persist install task-to-artifact meaning or make installer recovery discoverable after process exit.
helpers.head: c55d9ca619f6f9301ba1113615370fc6218d608f

integration_guidance: Extend the existing #660 ownership for scheduler replacement recovery; no competing open PR changes scheduler implementations or the snapshot regression test.
Keep #659 port-observation work independent. Shared filenames alone do not justify closing or combining PRs.
Reuse the existing owner-only secure-create/readback primitives if a fresh retained XML file is selected. Treat created=false and post-publication errors distinctly.
A persistent task-to-artifact descriptor/reference is still required if recovery must survive CLI rendering/process exit; existing client/Product journals are domain-specific.

RetainedTaskXMLMaterialStore is useful precedent but not automatically a qualified general immutable snapshot/leaf-cleanup owner. Its namespace, Windows-only surface, replacement behavior and leaf custody need an explicit fit decision.
Do not extend snapshot retention into a new storage framework or claim automatic restart recovery merely because bytes were written.
limits: Changed-file ownership is not exclusive semantic ownership.
No direct hunk overlap does not prove runtime/semantic compatibility or merge readiness.
Only selected helper source ranges and current shared-file patches were inspected; this was not a full-diff or security audit.
No build/test/native execution was performed; source behavior is not a runtime qualification.
No prior code was modified and no snapshot material was actually created.
No account details or PR/review/comment body text were retained.
